en.title: Hideki Kamiya says game preservation matters more to him than whether games are physical or digital
en.description: The Clovers co-founder buys games digitally, but wants companies to ensure older titles remain playable
en.fullContent:
The Clovers co-founder buys games digitally, but wants companies to ensure older titles remain playable

Okami, Devil May Cry, and Bayonetta creator Hideki Kamiya says he’s more concerned about the future of game preservation than whether games remain available physically or digitally.

Speaking alongside fellow Clovers co-founder Kento Koyama, Kamiya shared his thoughts with VGC over the impending end of physical game discs on PlayStation platforms.

Kamiya said that while the news doesn’t particularly affect his own buying habbits, since he now buys games “100% digital”, he does fear that something meaningful will be lost when physical games disappear.

“I don’t buy a single physical game these days – every single game I buy is 100% digital,” he said, “so I look at that decision and think, ‘Yeah, I guess this is where things were heading’.”

As a keen retro games collector, Kamiya said his bigger concern is whether games will remain available to play as hardware and distribution platforms change.

en.title: White House gives classic arcade games a MAGA makeover in new online launch
en.description: The White House is rolling out a new website Thursday featuring classic arcade-style games with a MAGA twist. (Credit: The White House)
en.fullContent:
The White House is rolling out a new website Thursday featuring classic arcade-style games with a MAGA twist. (Credit: The White House)

FIRST ON FOX: The White House is rolling out a new website Thursday that will feature classic arcade-style games with a MAGA twist.

A promotional video for the site obtained by Fox News Digital shows MAGA remakes of old favorites, including Snake, Flappy Bird, Duck Hunt and a couple of originals. Each one is uniquely Trumpian.

The MAGA version of Snake, for example, features border czar Tom Homan leading a line of illegal aliens in orange jumpsuits while he chases others on the grid. In another game, reminiscent of Duck Hunt, the user employs a net to catch gold bars and money, illustrative of putting money into a Trump Account. The Washington Monument is depicted in the background of that game.

The MAGA version of Snake from arcade.gov features Tom Homan capturing illegal aliens. (The White House)

SEN DAVE MCCORMICK: TRUMP ACCOUNTS GIVE ALL AMERICANS A STAKE IN PROSPERITY

en.title: 'Alien: Isolation 2': Facing a ruthless and evolved Xenomorph in our Gamescom hands-on preview
en.description: Sega and Creative Assembly's long-awaited survival horror sequel hits the ground running with a new cast of characters and a fast-paced prologue.
en.fullContent:
Sega and Creative Assembly's long-awaited survival horror sequel hits the ground running with a new cast of characters and a fast-paced prologue.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It's hard to downplay excitement for Alien: Isolation 2 after a first menacing teaser and promising early previews. Alien video games are in a good spot right now thanks to bangers like Aliens Dark Descent and Fireteam Elite 2, but nothing has hit quite like Creative Assembly's 2014 survival horror classic.

Now, after a thrilling Gamescom hands-on demo, it looks like the studio has nailed it once again, bringing Xenomorph-shaped scares to the next generation. At least that's what its breezy prologue section I played at Gamescom suggests.

As the earliest possible section of the game, no new mechanics were present, and the larger ideas and structure are still a big mystery. Instead, Sega and Creative Assembly have bet on pure atmosphere, dread that runs deeper thanks to more detailed graphics and audio, and of course, letting everyone know the Xenomorph's dynamic AI has evolved too.

Though it'd been mentioned before, the biggest shocker comes with the immediate reveal that Amanda Ripley is no longer the protagonist. Even if I wouldn't close the door on her showing up one way or another in Alien: Isolation 2, her story was continued elsewhere after all hope for a sequel was lost a few years ago. (Look at us now).

en.title: How 'GTA 6' looks on Xbox Series S: What we know
en.description: At the end of August, Rockstar Games treated us to our first official look at Grand Theft Auto VI gameplay. The only problem? It was captured on Pl...
en.fullContent:
At the end of August, Rockstar Games treated us to our first official look at Grand Theft Auto VI gameplay. The only problem? It was captured on PlayStation 5, leaving Xbox owners hanging.

That's not a huge deal in a vacuum, as every video game trailer has to be captured on something, and the game isn't coming to PC at launch. It's an issue because there are plenty of folks out there who own the Xbox Series S, the $500 slightly-less-powerful Xbox Series console that arguably represents the best value in the current-gen console space right now. Personally, I'd argue for the Switch 2, but GTA isn't coming to that, so it's a moot point in this context.

Anyway, you're wondering how GTA VI will look and play on Xbox Series S. Let's get into it.

Unfortunately, you know as much about the state of GTA on Series S as we do, at the time of publication. Rockstar has not divulged any information about that build of the game, nor has it been shown publicly. At best, we can look at the trailer captured on PS5 and make some educated guesses.

For example, if GTA VI is running at 30 frames per second on a regular PS5 (as it did in the trailer), it's certainly not going to run any faster than that on a Series S. At best, it'll be the same, but as we've seen with some Series S games over the years, there could be performance drawbacks in intense situations.

The same goes for resolution, which could be cut down on Series S. According to the video game tech experts at Digital Foundry, the PS5 trailer was running at a native 1440p. Most Series S games do not reach that level, and considering that Digital Foundry called GTA VI the most impressive real-time graphical rendering they'd ever seen, one can imagine it won't reach that resolution on Series S, either.

en.title: Bosses Concerned That GTA 6 Release Will Cause Massive Drop in Productivity
en.description: Can’t-miss innovations from the bleeding edge of science and tech
en.fullContent:
Can’t-miss innovations from the bleeding edge of science and tech

When the long awaited role playing game “Fallout 4” dropped in 2015, it marked the first installation in the franchise in five years. The release quickly became a running joke, with working class gamers yukking it up over their plans to call in sick the day it hit store shelves, and the game’s developer even issuing a bogus doctor’s note.

Now history seems to be repeating itself — and this time for almost certainly the most hyped game ever, making its release an actual liability for economy-wide productivity.

Enter “Grand Theft Auto VI,” the first installation in the beloved GTA franchise in 13 years. With nearly 5 million pre-orders worldwide, the game’s release on November 19 is poised to take a sizable chunk of the working population with it, a phenomenon tantamount to an unofficial holiday, as the Wall Street Journal tells it.

“We’ve got a couple of days where we’re like, ‘daddy’s very busy,'” Bud Burruss, a software engineer and father of three told the WSJ. When the game drops, Burruss said he plans on taking five whole days to himself.

“I’m not going to be playing it for, like, 20 hours straight like an absentee father,” the software engineer explained. “But right out of the gate we’re going hard. I’ll have the cave door shut.”
